#
# Note: The original LSF script did not request any specific resources like nodes

#

module load R

export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/home/ucl/eisuc058/code/abc-sysbio
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/home/ucl/eisuc058/code/cuda-sim

exe=/home/ucl/eisuc058/work/StabilityChecker/stabilitychecker
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/home/ucbtle1/cuda-sim-code


python $exe/my_abc.py -i input_file_pos_ab_tri.xml -o results_pos_ab_tri -l pos_ab_tri.log;# Rscript plot_posterior.R;

issues: The most critical resource-related issue is the lack of a GPU request. The script loads `cuda` and `pycuda` modules, which strongly implies it requires a GPU. However, no GPU is requested in the `#FLUX` resource directives (e.g., using `-g 1`). The job will fail if it is scheduled on a non-GPU node.

The script is missing explicit requests for cores (`-n` or `-c`) and memory. As noted in the comments, it will receive a small default allocation (typically 1 core and a small amount of memory). For a very long-running (100 hours) scientific computing job, this is a critical omission that will likely lead to poor performance or out-of-memory failures.

The script is extremely non-portable. It repeatedly modifies the `PYTHONPATH` with hardcoded, user-specific absolute paths. It also defines a variable `exe` with another hardcoded path. This makes the script impossible for anyone else to run and difficult for the original user to maintain.
The final command line has a commented-out R script call (`# Rscript ...`). This is confusing and suggests the script may be incomplete or that this part of the workflow is being skipped.
